correlation_note: This is the precondition that let the Act 1 phishing message through — see .pristine/mail-gateway.log's SPF_SOFTFAIL/POLICY_DECISION lines.

findings.title: DMARC policy is p=none (monitor-only)
findings.detail: DMARC is published but set to take no enforcement action on failing mail — spoofed/lookalike-domain mail is reported, never quarantined or rejected.
findings.recommended_fix: Move to p=quarantine, then p=reject, after confirming legitimate senders pass alignment.

findings.title: SPF uses ~all (soft-fail) instead of -all (hard-fail)
findings.detail: A soft-fail result is informational only for most mail gateways' default policy thresholds — it does not, by itself, block delivery.
findings.recommended_fix: Move to -all once all legitimate sending sources are enumerated in the SPF record.

findings.title: No attachment sandboxing/detonation for macro-enabled Office files
findings.detail: The gateway's macro scan is signature-based only (see mail-gateway.log's ATTACHMENT_SCAN line: 'engine=legacy-av-sig no-match-known-family') — no dynamic detonation is performed on suspicious-but-unmatched macros before delivery.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a sandboxing/detonation stage for macro-enabled attachments ahead of the signature engine.
